evals.prompt: I have a Rust CLI tool for managing container images. It has 18 files in src/ — all flat, no subdirectories. There's registry.rs (talks to Docker Hub API), oci.rs (OCI image spec parsing), cache.rs (local layer cache), manifest.rs (image manifest types), config.rs (CLI config + constants), pull.rs (orchestrates downloading layers), push.rs (orchestrates uploading), build.rs (builds images from Dockerfile), cli.rs (clap args), main.rs, error.rs, layer.rs (layer types + tar handling), auth.rs (registry auth), progress.rs (progress bars), digest.rs (sha256 digest type), platform.rs (os/arch filtering), and copy.rs (copies between registries). lib.rs just has 16 pub mod declarations. How should I restructure this?
evals.expected_output: Should evaluate the codebase first (asking questions about data flow, shared types, domain boundaries), identify it as primarily a phase-pipeline or domain-component architecture (not force layers), and propose grouping by domain responsibility — NOT a generic model/service/io layered structure
expectations: Evaluates the codebase architecture BEFORE proposing a structure (asks questions or analyzes data flow / dependency patterns)
Does NOT prescribe a generic layered architecture with model/service/transport or similar layer names as the primary grouping
Proposes grouping modules by domain responsibility or pipeline phase (e.g., registry/, image/, build/ or pull/push/build phases)
Identifies that types like digest, platform, layer belong with their domain, not in a catch-all types/ or model/ directory
Mentions keeping lib.rs skeletal with fewer top-level declarations (roughly 4-8)

evals.prompt: I'm building a Rust web API server with axum. Right now I have src/main.rs, routes.rs (all HTTP handlers, 800 lines), db.rs (all SQL queries, 600 lines), models.rs (all structs, 200 lines), auth.rs, and error.rs. The routes.rs file is a mess — it handles users, products, orders, and admin endpoints all in one file. How do I organize this?
evals.expected_output: Should recognize this as a layered/request-response architecture where layers DO make sense (handlers → service → storage), and recommend splitting the god module (routes.rs) by domain within the layer structure
expectations: Evaluates the codebase shape before prescribing structure (identifies the request/response boundary pattern)
Recognizes that a layered structure IS appropriate here (handlers/routes → business logic → database)
Recommends splitting routes.rs by domain (users, products, orders, admin) into separate files or a routes/ directory
Recommends splitting db.rs similarly by domain
Does NOT recommend the same structure that would be used for a CLI tool or pipeline tool — acknowledges this is a different kind of application

evals.prompt: We have a Rust package manager (like cargo but for a different ecosystem). The src/ tree has: manifest.rs (parses our manifest file), lockfile.rs (lockfile types + serialization), resolve.rs (dependency resolution with pubgrub), fetch.rs (downloads packages from registry), cache.rs (content-addressed cache), index.rs (registry index), staging.rs (prepares install directory), install.rs (copies to final location), cli.rs, error.rs, types.rs (ModuleId, PackageSpec, VersionReq — shared types used everywhere), and config.rs. Someone suggested we reorganize into model/ (types, manifest, lockfile, config), service/ (resolve, fetch, staging, install), and io/ (cache, index, registry HTTP). Is that a good idea?
evals.expected_output: Should explicitly reject or caution against the proposed model/service/io layered restructure for a pipeline tool, explain why phase-pipeline modules are better here, and warn about the 'model bag' anti-pattern
expectations: Explicitly advises against or cautions about the proposed model/service/io structure
Explains WHY layers are wrong here: scatters each pipeline phase across multiple directories, makes it hard to understand one phase end-to-end
Recommends keeping modules named after pipeline phases (resolve, fetch, cache, staging, install) or domain components
Warns about the 'model bag' anti-pattern — mixing ManifestFile, LockPackage, ModuleId, and config in one model/ directory
Suggests types.rs is acceptable IF kept small and focused on genuinely cross-cutting types, or recommends moving types to the modules that own them
